title: Acme Pay — payments platform (Container view)
caption: C4 container diagram, Acme Pay v3 architecture, as-is plus one proposed Settlement Service; Structurizr DSL.

spec.dsl:
workspace {
  model {
    customer = person "Customer"
    support = person "Support Agent"
    stripe = softwareSystem "Stripe (external)"
    plaid = softwareSystem "Plaid (external)"
    acmepay = softwareSystem "Acme Pay Platform" {
      web = container "Web App"
      api = container "Payments API"
      ledger = container "Ledger Service"
      db = container "Payments DB"
    }
    customer -> web "Sends and tracks payments"
    support -> web "Investigates disputes"
    web -> api "Calls over HTTPS"
    api -> ledger "Records double-entry txns"
    api -> db "Reads/writes payment state"
    api -> stripe "Authorizes and captures"
    api -> plaid "Links banks, checks balances"
  }
}

semantic_description.level_1_elemental: C4 container diagram (Structurizr DSL) of the Acme Pay payments platform. Two people (Customer, Support Agent), two external systems (Stripe, Plaid), and five containers inside the Acme Pay boundary: Web App (React), Payments API (Go), Ledger Service (Java), Transaction Store (PostgreSQL), and a dashed proposed Settlement Service (Go). Arrows are labeled with both an action and a technology.
semantic_description.level_2_statistical: 9 distinct elements drawn individually (4 outside the boundary, 5 containers inside) and 10 relationships. Three relationships and one container are tagged Proposed and render dashed; the remaining seven relationships are existing. The Payments API is the highest-degree node (4 connections: Web App, Ledger, Stripe, Plaid).
semantic_description.level_3_perceptual: Existing payment flow forms a single chain Customer -> Web App -> Payments API -> Ledger -> Transaction Store, with Stripe and Plaid hanging off the API. The dashed overlay surfaces the gap analysis: a proposed Settlement Service downstream of the Ledger that initiates Stripe payouts, plus a proposed direct Customer-to-Plaid bank-linking edge. The dashed elements cluster on the right/payout side, isolating what is missing from what already exists.
semantic_description.level_4_contextual: At container level the diagram shows that payment capture is built but bank settlement/payout is not yet owned in-house; the proposed Settlement Service closes that reconciliation-to-payout loop.
semantic_description.short_alt: C4 container diagram of Acme Pay: 2 users, 2 external systems, 5 containers, with a dashed proposed Settlement Service and Plaid link.
